item.title: Excelerate’s FSRU resumes operations, gas supply improves
item.description:
The floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), or LNG terminal, operated by Excelerate Energy at Maheshkhali in Cox’s Bazar, resumed gas supply today after a three-day shutdown.
Petrobangla Chairman Abdul Mannan said, “The FSRU resumed operations at around 2pm today and is currently supplying around 100 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas to the national grid.”
Gas supplied from the country’s two LNG terminals has pushed total LNG-based supply to around 686 mmcfd, while another nearly 300 mmcfd could be added to the national grid by midnight.
Mannan said an LNG cargo was scheduled to arrive on Sunday (Aug 23), but reached the terminal a day ahead of schedule. As a result, the terminal resumed supplying gas to the national grid today.
According to him, LNG-based gas supply stood at around 580 mmcfd at 2pm. Following the arrival of the new LNG cargo, the supply began to rise and has now reached around 686 mmcfd.
Summit is currently supplying around 580 mmcfd of the total LNG-based gas. Meanwhile, the country’s overall gas supply has increased to around 2,300 mmcfd.
“We are working to bring more cargoes to keep gas supply at a reliable level,” the Petrobangla chairman said.
Petrobangla said the Excelerate Energy LNG terminal at Maheshkhali was shut down following a fire on July 21. Although the terminal later resumed LNG supply, operations were suspended again on August 19 due to a lack of LNG cargo.

Lack of bridge leaves thousands suffering in Sariakandi
item.description:
Thousands of people in Bohail and Karnibari unions of Sariakandi upazila are suffering due to the lack of a bridge or footbridge over a canal at Johorer Ghat, near the Madarganj border in Jamalpur.
Residents have been using a boat to cross the canal for years, putting their lives and belongings at risk. They say essential goods frequently fall into the water, while accidents involving passengers and motorcycles are also common.
Local residents have urged the authorities to construct a bridge or a sturdy footbridge over the roughly 200-metre canal to ease their daily commute.
Jahida Begum, 65, of Uttar Shankarpur village in Bohail union, recently experienced the danger firsthand.
She said she fell into the water while getting off a boat after returning from Madarganj and lost her gold bangles and nose ring.
“I fell into the water while getting off the boat. I lost my bangles and nose ring, but despite searching later, I could not find them,” she said.
Residents said people from Bohail and Karnibari generally travel to Madarganj for their daily necessities because the Jamuna River makes travelling to Sariakandi upazila headquarters difficult.
The road connecting the area to Madarganj was washed away many years ago, creating the canal. Since then, residents have been relying on the boat service at Johorer Ghat.
Locals said students, farmers and other commuters are among those suffering the most.
College students sometimes fall into the water and damage their clothes, while some avoid attending educational institutions because of the risky crossing. Farmers also risk losing fertilizer, seeds and pesticides when they fall into the water.
Motorcyclists have also fallen into the canal and sustained injuries, residents said.
Ahsan Habib, a resident of Karnibari union, said thousands of people and numerous motorcycles use Johorer Ghat every day to travel to Madarganj.
“Although we are residents of Sariakandi upazila, we have remained neglected because the area is located near the border of Madarganj in Jamalpur. There is still no bridge or footbridge here,” he said.
He urged the administrations of Sariakandi and Madarganj to take immediate steps to construct a bridge at the ghat.
Sariakandi Upazila Nirbahi Officer SM Mikail Islam said the administration was aware of the longstanding problem.
He said thousands of people from Bohail and Karnibari unions use the canal crossing to travel to Madarganj, particularly because of the geographical difficulties created by the Jamuna River.
“We will discuss the construction of a bridge or footbridge with the relevant authorities of Jamalpur district and send a report,” he said.
The UNO also advised residents to submit a formal application regarding the construction of the bridge.
“Based on their application, the Sariakandi upazila administration will take steps to construct a sturdy footbridge there as soon as possible,” he added.

item.title: Jute prices fall in Narail, farmers fear losses
item.description:
Jute farmers in Narail are struggling as prices of the crop have fallen by around Tk1,000 per maund in just 15 days.
According to sources, jute that fetched Tk4,200-Tk4,600 per maund at the beginning of the season is now selling for Tk3,200-Tk3,600, depending on quality, leaving farmers worried about recovering their production costs.
Farmers said the cost of cultivation has risen at every stage, including land preparation, seed, fertiliser, irrigation, weed control, harvesting, retting, fibre extraction, washing, drying and transportation.
Rising labour and transport costs have further increased production expenses, making it difficult for farmers to make a reasonable profit at current market prices.
According to the district agriculture office, jute has been cultivated on 23,517 hectares in Narail this season, with a production target of 58,198 tonnes. Harvesting has already been completed on around 98% of the cultivated land.
The large volume of newly harvested jute entering the market at the same time has increased supply, putting downward pressure on prices.
At Tularampur and Mithapur haats, two of the district's major jute markets, farmers were seen bringing jute from different areas from early morning.
Traders were assessing the jute based on its colour, fibre quality, moisture content and drying condition before setting prices. After negotiations, the purchased jute was being transported to warehouses.
Abdul Halim, a jute farmer from Itna, said he received a good price at the beginning of the season but is now struggling to sell his produce at a profitable rate.
“We are facing the same costs we incurred during cultivation, but the price of jute has fallen sharply. If prices continue to decline, we may not even recover our production costs,” he said.
Some farmers alleged that a section of middlemen and traders were taking advantage of increased supply to buy jute at lower prices. They called for regular market monitoring to ensure fair competition.
Farmers have also complained about irregularities in weighing.
According to them, although a maund is conventionally considered to be 40kg, some buyers are allegedly counting 42kg as one maund. This means farmers have to provide an additional 2kg of jute for every maund, further increasing their losses.
The farmers fear prices could fall further as more jute reaches the market. They said prolonged low prices could discourage farmers from cultivating jute in the future.
The district agriculture office said supply has increased as harvesting has nearly finished across the district. It stressed the need to ensure fair prices for farmers.
Farmers have called for stronger market monitoring, accurate weighing and effective measures to ensure they receive a fair price for their produce.
Narail Deputy Commissioner Dr Mohammad Abdul Salam said the administration was monitoring the jute market.
He said action would be taken if any syndicate or market manipulation was found to be harming farmers.
“The complaints regarding weighing will also be investigated. If any irregularity or manipulation is found, legal action will be taken,” he said.
Mohammad Arifur Rahman, deputy director of the DAE in Narail, said both cultivation and yield have been good this year.
“Favourable weather and timely support from the agriculture department, including quality seeds, fertiliser and technical advice, have contributed to good cultivation and yield,” he said.
However, he acknowledged that fluctuations in jute prices are worrying farmers. “We are regularly advising farmers on improving the quality of jute fibre,” he said.

item.title: ‘Towhidi Janata’ demands halt to traditional boat race in Sylhet
item.description:
A group using the banner ‘Towhidi Janata’ has called for a traditional boat race on the Sunai River in Sylhet’s Beanibazar to be cancelled, setting up a dispute with organisers who say the event will go ahead on Aug 28.
According to sources, local youths from Lauta and Bahadur villages have been preparing for the annual boat race, which traditionally attracts thousands of spectators and creates a festive atmosphere in the riverside communities.
A group calling itself ‘Towhidi Janata’ held a meeting at Barigram Bazar Mosque last Thursday and demanded that the boat race be stopped.
Local residents said the race has been a longstanding source of entertainment and is held every year. The opposition to this year’s event has sparked discussion and tension in the area.
Former Lauta Union Parishad chairman Gaus Uddin said efforts were underway to resolve the issue through discussions with both sides and prevent any escalation.
Lauta Union Parishad Chairman Delwar Hossain said he had seen discussions for and against the event on Facebook but had no further information.
Beanibazar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Umme Habiba Majumder said she had looked into the matter after learning about the cancellation demand.
According to her, the opposing group cited a killing that occurred in connection with last year’s boat race as the reason for their demand.
However, the UNO said the boat race is a traditional sport and the administration would provide necessary support if the organizers obtain permission and inform the authorities and law enforcement agencies.
Beanibazar police said the situation was being monitored and that the UNO was working to address the issue.

item.title: DNCC launches special cleanliness week drive
item.description:
Dhaka North City Corporation’s (DNCC) cleanliness campaign will not be confined to a single day but will continue as an ongoing process, with greater public awareness needed to make Dhaka a clean city, DNCC Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan said.
He made the remarks while inaugurating a special cleanliness week program in front of the DNCC Regional Office at Mohakhali in the capital yesterday, said a press release.
Shafiqul Islam said the cleanliness week initiative has been launched across all DNCC zones as part of a long-term plan announced by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to build a “Clean Dhaka, Green Dhaka.”
“Keeping Dhaka clean cannot be achieved through a one-day campaign. It must be a continuous process, and public awareness is essential to its success,” he said, adding that sanitation workers at the ward and unit levels are performing their regular duties every day according to their assigned schedules.
He noted that DNCC covers a vast geographical area and serves a densely populated city, making it impossible for the corporation alone to ensure cleanliness across the entire area. “Along with ensuring civic services, we also expect active cooperation from citizens,” he said.
He urged people to stop throwing tissues, plastic and other waste indiscriminately in public places. “Everyone should take responsibility for keeping their homes and the areas in front of their residences clean. If citizens cooperate, we will be able to achieve our cleanliness targets ahead of schedule,” he said.

item.title: Moyeen Khan: Cabinet expansion aims to make Bangladesh a dynamic state
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan has said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has taken charge of Bangladesh at a critical juncture in its history with a mandate from the people, pledging to advance the country on the path of democracy and restore people’s rights.
He made the remarks while speaking to journalists after paying tribute to the martyrs at the National Memorial in Savar on Saturday.
Regarding the induction of new members into the cabinet, Dr Moyeen Khan said the move was part of a normal process following the formation of the cabinet six months ago. “Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has taken charge of the country with the votes of millions of Bangladeshis. After 17 years of authoritarian rule, he has dedicated himself to advancing Bangladesh towards democracy and establishing the rights of the people.”
He further said the cabinet expansion was aimed at addressing the country’s challenges and making Bangladesh a more dynamic state. “The prime minister is fully aware of the problems and issues facing Bangladesh. This initiative has been taken to resolve those problems, make Bangladesh a dynamic state and restore the country’s reputation in the global community,” he added.
Referring to the declaration of independence by BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman, Dr Khan said Ziaur Rahman made the declaration from the Kalurghat Radio Centre at a critical moment when the nation was facing uncertainty.
He stressed the need to present such historical events to the younger generation, saying Bangladesh’s democratic journey had been disrupted repeatedly and that the BNP had consistently worked to restore democracy.
The minister also highlighted the political role of former BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, saying she established herself as an uncompromising leader during the political crisis of the 1980s and was elected Bangladesh’s first female prime minister through a popular vote in 1991.

item.title: Two-hour power outage disrupts services at CMCH
item.description:
A two-hour power outage at Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH) on Saturday caused inconvenience to patients and their attendants, disrupting diagnostic and other routine services.
The hospital remained without electricity from 9:30 am to 11:30 am, affecting services at the emergency department and other units. Patients waiting to collect tickets, undergo diagnostic tests and receive treatment faced prolonged delays.
The Department of Radiology and Imaging, which has six X-ray machines, was among the units affected. X-ray examinations were suspended during the outage, leaving patients waiting for power to be restored.
Kazi Md Alam, head of the department, said X-ray services could not be provided during the outage. “Ultrasonography machines also require air conditioning to operate. Since there was no electricity, those machines could not be kept running either,” he said.
Shahidul Islam, executive engineer of the Power Development Board (PDB), said the outage was caused by scheduled maintenance work. “An announcement had been made the previous day that cabling and repair work would be carried out on a feeder under the Stadium area. As a result, power supply to the area was temporarily suspended,” he said.
However, he said the supply was restored after the hospital director contacted him and requested immediate action, citing the difficulties faced by patients.
CMCH Director Brigadier General Md Taslim Uddin said the hospital’s generator system kept essential medical services operational during the outage. “Critical facilities, including the operation theatres, emergency department, surgery wards, ICU, CCU and HDU, remained operational through generator power,” he said.
According to the director, the outage did not cause any major disruption to critical treatment, although some routine diagnostic services were temporarily affected.

Bangladesh confirmed for inaugural FIFA Asean Cup
item.description:
Bangladesh will take part in the inaugural FIFA Asean Cup, scheduled to be held from September 24 to October 4 this year, the Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) confirmed following its executive committee meeting in Dhaka on Saturday.
The FIFA Asean Cup is a FIFA-sanctioned international football competition for Southeast Asian men's national teams and invited guest nations.
The tournament will feature a two-division format, with Indonesia hosting the Premier Division and Hong Kong hosting the Challenge Division.
Bangladesh have been included in the Premier Division.
Eight teams, divided into two groups, will compete in the tournament.
According to BFF executive committee member Amirul Islam Babu, Bangladesh have been drawn in Group A alongside hosts Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. Group B consists of Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Pakistan.
All Premier Division matches will be played in Jakarta, Indonesia.
"We received confirmation from FIFA yesterday that we are going to play in the Asean Cup," Babu told reporters on Saturday.
The tournament will be held during the FIFA international window from September 24 to October 4.
Babu also said preparations for the competition would begin soon.
"The squad will be announced very soon according to the coach's plans and recommendations," he added.

item.title: CNG drivers lose half day in gas queues, earnings plunge
item.description:
The gas shortage continues to cause severe hardship for CNG-run autorickshaw and other gas-powered vehicle drivers in Dhaka, with many spending hours in long queues at filling stations without getting enough fuel.
The shortage is eroding their daily earnings while making it increasingly difficult to meet their fixed daily payments to vehicle owners.
The situation was observed during visits to CNG filling stations across the capital on Saturday, where drivers and station officials spoke about the worsening crisis.
Drivers said they often have to wait up to three hours for gas at many stations. Even after the long wait, some stations are limiting sales. In some cases, drivers said they had to return to the road after hours of waiting with as little as Tk 120 worth of gas.
The prolonged queues are cutting into their working hours and increasing operating costs, they said. With earnings falling, many are struggling to meet their daily payments to vehicle owners.
CNG driver Md Mona said he had been waiting in a queue since 4am.
“I had to borrow money to pay the vehicle owner. I still haven’t got gas. How will I pay the owner and run my family? I also have to pay my house rent soon,” he said.
Another driver, Jahangir, said he pays Tk 1,200 to the vehicle owner every day and needs about Tk 500 worth of gas.
“I spend another Tk 200-250 on my own expenses. So my daily costs come to Tk 1,500-2,000. My income has virtually stopped for the past two months because of the gas shortage,” he said.
No daytime supply, limited gas at night
Kamal, manager of MA Masud Filling Station in Uttara, said the gas crisis had worsened, with no supply available during the day.
“There is not enough pressure for regular supply. The pressure is so low that we cannot operate our valves. Only stations whose valves can operate at low pressure are able to provide some gas,” he said.
He said some gas was available at night, while pressure generally began to improve in the afternoon.
“There is no good news about the gas situation. We don’t know when it will return to normal. Although we get some gas at night, we cannot supply it throughout the day,” said Tarek, an employee of Akij CNG Station.
Abdullah, an employee of Zaman Station, also said they received some gas at night but no supply during the day.
Private-car driver Sanuallah said, “We are going through extremely difficult times. We cannot work, but our expenses continue.”
Long queues at stations across Dhaka
Visits to filling stations in Uttara’s Abdullahpur, the airport area, Khilkhet and other parts of the capital found many stations closed due to the shortage.
Even at stations that remained open, low pressure was preventing normal supply, forcing CNG-run vehicles, trucks and other gas-powered vehicles to wait for hours.
Long queues were seen at Khandakar Filling Station in Abdullahpur and several stations in the Airport-Khilkhet area.
Monir Hossain, an operator at Khandakar Filling Station, said the station had not received adequate gas for the past two weeks. “If we don’t have gas, how can we supply customers? CNG drivers are leaving without gas. Our station is completely closed,” he said.
A similar situation was found at RSR Filling Station on the western side of Abdullahpur along the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway. “We had some gas pressure around 1pm, but it disappeared shortly afterwards,” said sales employee Zainul Alam.
Long queues were also seen at Russell Filling and CNG Station and Haji CNG Filling Station in Demra. At Russell, only one of four hoses could be kept operational due to low pressure.
At Haji Filling Station in Mirpara, gas was being supplied through a single hose on a limited scale.
“We have come all the way from Jatrabari to Demra to get gas. Are we supposed to starve with our families?” said CNG driver Md Sarwar Arif. Similar scenes were reported in Mohakhali, Tejgaon, Kawran Bazar, Satrasta, Malibagh, Motijheel, Maniknagar, Khilgaon, Sabujbagh, Banasree and Goran.
Akij CNG Station at the busy Satrasta intersection was closed, with a sign reading “No Gas” displayed at the entrance. Tarek, a guard and nozzleman at the station, said it had been shut due to the shortage.
At ABN CNG Filling Station in the Mohakhali bus stand area, manager Shahidul said the pressure was so low that the pump automatically shut down after operating for a short time.
“After waiting for a while, it starts again. This is how we are managing to provide limited supply,” he said.
Long queues were also seen at several stations in Malibagh, including Malibagh Hajipara CNG Fueling Station, Shanto CNG Refuelling Station on Bishwaroad, NS CNG Filling and Servicing Centre on RK Mission Road and Best Eastern CNG Filling Station in Maniknagar.
Drivers demand immediate solution
Drivers fear that thousands of people dependent on gas-powered vehicles will suffer further financial losses if the crisis persists.
Their livelihoods depend on driving, but without adequate gas, they cannot operate their vehicles or support their families.
People concerned with the sector said the recent crisis was triggered by delays in LNG unloading due to maintenance work at a terminal in Maheshkhali, along with reduced gas supplies to the national grid.
The shortage has affected residential consumers, CNG drivers and industries alike.
The government has said the situation is expected to improve significantly within a few days. Drivers, however, are demanding immediate and effective measures to bring the crisis under control.

item.description:
Health officials on Saturday said they recorded 702 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 702) 115 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 107 in Chittagong division, 47 in Dhaka division, 88 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 123 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 114 in Khulna division, 38 in Mymensingh division, 54 in Rajshahi division and 15 in Rangpur division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaught in Bangladesh, this year witnessed so far 77 deaths, while the disease inflicted 28,090 people.
Last year, the mosquito-borne disease claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country, while it claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: CDA to build tourist zone at Karnaphuli bank in Chittagong
item.description:
Chittagong Development Authority (CDA) is set to establish a three-kilometer tourist zone on the bank of the Karnaphuli River in Bakalia region of the port city.
This initiative will be implemented under a project named "Construction of Road on the bank of River Karnaphuli from Kalurghat bridge to Chaktai Khal (canal)."
CDA’s chief town planner Abu Issa Anshary informed BSS that a walkway will also be constructed over a five-kilometer area extending from Shah Amanat Bridge to Bolirhat. Additionally, a restaurant catering to tourists and a complete entertainment options for children will be built. The funds allocated for this project will be utilized to create various tourist attractions, he noted. Local resident Jabed Ahmed remarked: "The socio-economic conditions of this area will improve significantly if the tourism zone is established." He further stated that Chittagong and its neighboring upazilas possess numerous features that appeal to tourists, such as stunning sea views, mountains, mangrove forests, waterfalls, and lakes.
However, the potential of many tourist sites has largely gone unexploited due to the lack of interest from the government agencies.
Architect Shahinul Islam Khan, the former chief urban planner of the CDA, emphasized the necessity for authorities to maintain the cleanliness of the river. He stated that establishing an eco-friendly tourist center in this area would significantly transform the port city into a genuine tourist destination. Data from the CDA indicates that the project received approval during a meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on April 25, 2017. The construction phase of the project commenced on June 2019 with the initiation of a sluice gate at the estuary of the Chaktai canal. Project Director Rajib Das stated: "Upon completion of the construction, this road will link the Dhaka-Chittagong and Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar highways via the City Bypass Loop Road and the Oxygen-Quaish Link Road, thereby alleviating traffic congestion within the city." He further explained that vehicles arriving from Kaptai, Rangunia, and Boalkhali upazilas will be able to bypass the city center using this road, facilitating access to the city’s airport, Patenga area, and southern Chittagong. Tourists from Chittagong city, as well as the northern and southern districts, will soon be able to enjoy the tourist zone. He additionally stated that 92% of the construction for this 9.5-kilometer-long road has been finalized. The remaining tasks are anticipated to be completed by December. Once the road is fully functional, it will offer numerous advantages, he added.
So, it will open up new opportunities for managing waterlogging in the city, safeguarding riverbanks, enhancing urban connectivity, establishing a modern water drainage system, and promoting the tourism industry.
CDA chairman engineer Belayet Hossain informed BSS that the project has been incorporated into the CDA Master Plan, with plans to establish a three-kilometer-long tourist zone. Efforts are underway to develop these areas through private or joint venture initiatives.
He mentioned that a walkway extending over three kilometers from Shah Amanat Bridge to Bolirhat will be constructed, along with a tourist center on both the sides of Marine Drive. A family-friendly restaurant featuring entertainment options for children will be established, he said. The CDA chairman noted that Bakalia is regarded as one of the less developed regions of Chittagong city.
Urban planners assert that the successful execution of this plan could significantly transform the area's landscape. item.title: Humaiun: No rush on PM’s India visit, national interest comes first
item.description:
Newly appointed State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Saturday said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit India at an appropriate time following progress in discussions, with the country’s national interests being given priority.
He said the government wants to maintain a positive and effective relationship with India, but Bangladesh cannot move forward with relations with any country by compromising its national interests.
The state minister made the remarks while responding to queries from journalists after paying homage to the Liberation War martyrs at the National Memorial in Savar at noon.
Regarding relations with India, he said, “We want a positive relationship with India. Why wouldn’t we? They are our neighbours. We should have an effective relationship.”
However, Kobir said there will be no compromise on Bangladesh’s national interests. “Not only with India, but with no country can we do anything by compromising our national interests,” he said.
About extradition of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, he said she went to India after fleeing Bangladesh following her involvement in the killing of 1,500 people during the July 2024 mass uprising, and that judicial proceedings in several cases against her have already reached conclusions, while many other cases remain pending.
The state minister said Bangladesh has an extradition treaty with India. “So, these are not new conditions or a new kind of engagement; these are ongoing issues,” he said.
He said bringing back Hasina and other alleged offenders who fled to India is linked to the expectations of the people of Bangladesh.
“There are more criminals who have fled to India. This is a natural demand of the people of Bangladesh and a matter of their sentiment. We want to engage with India by giving priority to this process,” Kobir said.
“We will engage with India. We want a positive relationship. But it has to be done by prioritising Bangladesh’s national interests,” he said, adding that there is no rush over the Prime Minister’s India visit.
“If we reach an agreement based on our national interests tomorrow, we can go [to India] next week, or the week after. There is no rush here,” the state minister said.
He said necessary preparations and discussions are required before a visit at the prime ministerial level.
“There are issues to discuss and preparations to make. A prime ministerial-level visit is not something that can just happen suddenly. This is not a game,” Kobir said.
He said the two sides need to establish the necessary preparations and groundwork before a meeting between the heads of government. “We are doing exactly that,” he said.
The state minister said Bangladesh is receiving indications of a positive attitude and goodwill from India, noting that it has also acknowledged the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh.
“You can see that statements are also coming from India on this issue. They have acknowledged that the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh have been hurt, particularly by Sheikh Hasina’s press conference on August 5 this year. They have taken note of the matter,” he said, describing this as a “good beginning.”
“Now let us see whether there is some progress in the remaining discussions. Based on the discussions and our national interests, we will certainly visit India when the time is appropriate,” Kobir said.

item.title: Swapon: Yellow journalism increasingly blurs media standards
item.description:
Former Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Saturday said the distinction between yellow and responsible journalism is increasingly becoming blurred, posing a major challenge for the media industry.
“The gap between yellow and responsible journalism has become increasingly pronounced, while the line distinguishing the two is gradually disappearing,” he said.
Swapon made the remarks while inaugurating the annual District Correspondents’ Conference of United News of Bangladesh (UNB) 2026 at the Cosmos Centre in Malibagh.
Speaking about the changing media landscape, he said readership of print newspapers is declining as people are increasingly becoming device-oriented, while digital platforms have gained widespread dominance.
He said the key challenge for both traditional and digital media is to ensure that information remains objective as it moves from limited sources to a vast number of platforms.
Swapon urged responsible journalists to help curb yellow journalism and separate mainstream media from what he described as “parasitic media” and “digital junk”.
He also highlighted the need to distinguish investigative journalism from an intelligence-gathering mindset and urged the media to move from event-based reporting towards knowledge-based and comprehensive journalism.
He identified “objectivity versus instant sensation” as another major challenge in the digital era, warning that the rush to break news could undermine a media organization’s credibility.
“The credibility and credentials of a media organization are like glass. They can break or develop a crack in a single incident,” he said.
Swapon also called for stronger attention to journalists’ wages, job security and working conditions, stressing the importance of compliance with the Wage Board. He said media owners must ensure proper salary structures, job security, a safe working environment and gender equality.
He also called for clear editorial policies and an appropriate regulatory framework for the media industry.
Swapon said he hoped his successor, Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho, would maintain continuity in the sector. He also said he is likely to move as an adviser on media and related issues to the prime minister’s Office.
UNB Editor-in-Chief Enayetullah Khan welcomed the participants at the conference. Several senior journalists, media professionals and officials also spoke at the event.

item.title: Amir Khosru: Higher education must be linked to employment, entrepreneurship
item.description:
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Friday called for linking higher education with employment and entrepreneurship, urging authorities to consider priority sectors, employment prospects and entrepreneurial opportunities while establishing new universities and introducing new faculties and subjects.
“Higher education subjects and curricula must be determined in line with the country’s economic needs and labour market realities. The goal of higher education should not be limited to obtaining certificates; it should also prepare students for employment and entrepreneurship,” he said.
The minister was addressing the ‘Vice-Chancellors' Dialogue: Shaping the Future of Higher Education’, a two-day national policy dialogue organised under the Higher Education Acceleration and Transformation (HEAT) Project of the University Grants Commission (UGC) at BRAC CDM in Savar.
He also stressed the need for stronger university-industry collaboration, saying universities and industries in many countries maintain close links and Bangladesh should utilise the potential of such cooperation.
“Why can’t we develop industry-university interaction in Bangladesh? Around the world, universities and industries are seriously connected. We need to utilise this potential,” he said.
Amir Khosru said international and national rankings of higher education institutions have an impact not only on employment opportunities and global recognition but also on the overall image of a country.
He urged universities to identify the reasons behind the weak university-industry linkage and the mismatch between education and labour market requirements.
“Why can’t we change our education system in relation to the job market?” he asked, stressing the need to establish a stronger relationship between education and employment.
The minister also underscored the importance of research as a fundamental component of higher education and called for linking research with industry.
“Research is fundamental for education. We need to determine our priorities in research and explore how we can connect research with industry,” he said.
He urged universities to conduct research to address real-life problems faced by industries and businesses and called upon the private sector to finance university research and commercially utilise research findings.
“Research should not remain confined to publications; it must contribute to national development and people’s welfare,” he said.
Questioning the academic structure of newly established universities, Amir Khosru said their faculties and academic programmes should be selected based on specific educational, regional and employment needs.
“I do not know under what consideration these faculties have been selected. I don’t see the reason,” he said. He said establishing new universities was a positive development, but their academic programmes should be designed to address the needs of the regions where they are located.
“What target are we trying to fulfil through these universities? Do people in those areas have proper opportunities to enter the job market?” he asked.
He said newly established universities have an advantage as they could be designed from the beginning to address existing challenges in higher education.
The minister said he would request the UGC to formulate appropriate guidelines on the faculties and subjects to be introduced at newly established universities, taking into account regional needs, priority sectors and employment opportunities.

item.title: Drive begins to revive navigability of Old Buriganga
item.description:
A massive cleanliness drive began on Friday at the Durani canal and adjacent areas to revive the navigability of the Old Buriganga channel, a 7-kilometre historical waterway near Kamrangirchar and Rasulpur in Dhaka.
The Dhaka district administration, along with volunteer-based youth organization "BD Clean", jointly launched the drive.
The drive began following the Prime Minister’s directive to State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives, Mir Shahe Alam, to revive the channel after removing waste dumps.
In line with the directive, initiatives have been taken for re-excavation, eviction drives and dredging projects to revive the blocked waterway, restore navigability and build modern civic walkways.
Before starting the drive, the LGRD state minister administered an oath to stakeholders, including members of BD Clean.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator M Abdus Salam, Hamidur Rahman, MP of Dhaka-7, and Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanam were also present.
A cleanliness drive is launched at the Durani canal and adjacent areas to revive the navigability of the Old Buriganga channel in Dhaka on Friday, August 21, 2026. Photo: BSS
Approximately 1,000 feet of the 3.2-km-long Old Buriganga channel, the oldest water channel in Old Dhaka, located around the Durani Bridge area, as well as different parts of the channel, have become waste-dumping sites due to land encroachment.
The obstruction of water flow, along with bad smells, mosquito menace and waterlogging, has caused immense suffering to local residents.
According to experts, the normal water flow of the Old Buriganga channel was hampered following the construction of the Dhaka flood-control embankment, widely known as the Beribadh, in the early 1990s to protect the western and northern parts of the city from seasonal river floods.
Under the circumstances, the government has taken a fresh initiative to make the channel an eco-friendly and public-friendly water body.
Waste disposal inside the channel and its adjacent areas has begun, while an awareness programme is also being conducted among local people, urging them not to dump waste at the waterway.
After completion of the cleanliness drive, initiatives will be taken to restore the navigability of the channel, said DSCC sources, adding that beautification will be carried out on both sides of the channel and civic walkways will also be constructed for the recreation of local residents.
Inaugurating the cleanliness drive, the state minister said: “It is imperative to keep canals and rivers free from waste to protect the environment and public health. The joint initiative of the Dhaka district administration and BD Clean is praiseworthy.”
“We hope that the programme will be successfully completed and local people will benefit from it,” he added.
Alongside the cleanliness drive, the Dhaka district administration will maintain surveillance to ensure that the channel is not encroached upon or polluted again.

item.title: Three top criminals arrested in Mohammadpur
item.description:
Rapid Action Battalion (RAB-2) has arrested three alleged criminals, including a teen gang member, in separate raids in the capital’s Mohammadpur area.
The arrestees are Mohammad Selim Ashrafi alias Chua Selim, a top drug dealer and alleged criminal from Geneva Camp; Joy, second-in-command of the Mahi teen gang; and Mohammad Ratan alias Boma Ratan, a listed criminal.
RAB-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan disclosed the information at a press briefing at the battalion’s Basila office on Friday.
He said Chua Selim, accused in 36 cases and wanted in murder and drug-related cases, was arrested from Geneva Camp with a foreign-made pistol, two rounds of ammunition and 110 grams of heroin.
According to RAB, Chua Selim had long been involved in drug trafficking, mugging, murder, clashes and other criminal activities in and around Geneva Camp. He was previously arrested from Dhanmondi on January 8 last year.
On the same day, RAB-2 arrested Joy from Chand Udyan. He is accused in 10 cases involving robbery, mugging and drug-related offences.
RAB said Joy and other members of the Mahi gang had long been involved in mugging, extortion and assaults in Dhaka Udyan, Chand Udyan and Nabinagar, creating fear among residents. Local businesspeople, tenants and construction workers were allegedly regular targets of extortion.
Joy was also arrested by law enforcement agencies from Mohammadpur on April 24 this year.
In a separate operation, RAB-2 arrested listed criminal Mohammad Ratan alias Boma Ratan from Bijli Mohalla in Mohammadpur.
Ratan is accused in 20 cases involving robbery, dacoity, mugging and arms offences, RAB said.
According to the elite force, Boma Ratan had long led an armed gang involved in robbery, mugging and other criminal activities in Gaznabi Road, Basila and Geneva Camp.
He was previously detained with a sharp weapon from Gaznabi Road on February 19, 2022.

LDP Chairman and 11-party alliance presidential candidate Dr Col (retd) Oli Ahmed on Thursday congratulated Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his election as the 23rd president of Bangladesh.

item.title: Private clinics mushroom across Naogaon, raising regulatory concerns
item.description:
Private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres have mushroomed across Naogaon’s 11 upazilas, raising concerns over facilities allegedly operating without proper documents and approvals.
Many of these establishments have reportedly been operating for years despite lacking the required paperwork, while authorities often appear to step up enforcement only after serious incidents, including patient deaths allegedly linked to medical negligence.
Once administrative drives subside, however, some of the facilities reportedly resume operations.
Several private establishments also lack the infrastructure and environment required to provide proper medical care, raising concerns about patient safety.
The proliferation of private facilities around government upazila health complexes has added to the problem. Patients and locals allege that brokers representing private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres remain stationed around government hospitals to divert patients to private facilities.
There are also allegations that some doctors working at government health complexes have arrangements with private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres.
Patients from remote areas seeking treatment at government facilities are sometimes allegedly pushed into undergoing unnecessary diagnostic tests, even when they seek treatment for common ailments.
Patients have also complained about the behaviour of some government doctors, shortages of medicines and the irregular availability of physicians. They said these problems have contributed to growing dissatisfaction with government healthcare services.
By contrast, private facilities are often perceived as offering more attentive care and better treatment to patients in exchange for payment, encouraging more people to seek treatment there.
According to the Naogaon Civil Surgeon’s Office, the district has 115 registered private hospitals and clinics across its 11 upazilas. Naogaon Sadar has the highest number, with 43.
An application has recently been submitted to establish a facility named Science Lab and Hospital in Naogaon Sadar.
Meanwhile, Ekta Clinic at Saraigachhi intersection in Porsha and Porsha Islami Lab and Hospital have been ordered to shut down, according to the Civil Surgeon’s Office.
Civil Surgeon Dr Md Aminul Islam said the health department was working to bring greater transparency to the district’s healthcare sector.
“Whenever we receive allegations or find irregularities involving private hospitals, clinics or diagnostic centres, we conduct drives and take immediate action,” he said.
He said the district’s healthcare services had improved significantly compared with the past.
The health department would continue its efforts to eliminate irregularities, the civil surgeon said, urging people with specific complaints to submit them in writing so authorities could investigate and take appropriate action.

item.title: 82% of children who died from measles lacked exclusive breastfeeding
item.description:
About 82% of children who died while undergoing treatment for measles had not received adequate or exclusive breastfeeding during their first 6 months of life, according to a joint study by Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute and icddr,b.
The findings were presented at a dissemination meeting on the study at the auditorium of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
The study was conducted among 354 children hospitalized with measles and is still ongoing, researchers said.
According to the study, 40% of the affected children were aged between 3 and 9 months. Overall, 38% had not received exclusive breastfeeding during the first 6 months of life.
The proportion was significantly higher among children who died while undergoing treatment, with 82% not having received exclusive breastfeeding during their first 6 months.
Researchers also analyzed the nutritional status of the children. The study found that 65% of measles-affected children were malnourished, including 12% with severe malnutrition and 53% with moderate malnutrition.
For an analysis based on age and vaccination status, researchers divided 341 children into 4 groups.
Among 146 children under 9 months of age who were not yet eligible for routine measles vaccination, 142 tested positive for measles, representing 97.3%.
Among 126 children who were eligible for vaccination but had not received any dose, 122 tested positive, or 97%.
Of the 48 children who had received 1 dose of vaccine, 44 tested positive for measles, representing 92%. Meanwhile, 16 of the 21 children who had received the recommended 2 doses tested positive, accounting for 76%.
Researchers cautioned that the finding does not mean that 76% of children who receive 2 doses of measles vaccine contract the disease.
The study was not conducted among the general population. Instead, it focused on a specific group of children admitted to hospital with suspected measles.
Therefore, the finding that 16 of the 21 suspected cases who had received 2 doses tested positive requires further investigation, researchers said.
The study noted that several factors may contribute to infection despite vaccination, including inadequate development of immunity after vaccination, waning antibody protection over time, malnutrition and other individual health-related factors.
However, determining the extent to which each factor contributed to infection was beyond the scope of the current study.
Researchers also analyzed the measles virus detected among the affected children. All the viruses identified belonged to the B3 subclade and showed similarities with B3 viruses detected in other countries.
The researchers also identified 4 changes or mutations in the epitope region of the virus's H protein, which can be recognized by antibodies.
The research was conducted under the Epidemiology and Research Department of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute.
The main research paper was presented by the institute's Director Professor Dr Mirza Mohammad Ziaul Islam and icddr,b Senior Director Dr Mustafizur Rahman.
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit attended the dissemination meeting as the chief guest, while Professor Dr AKM Azizul Haque, chairman of the governing board of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute, chaired the event.
Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services Professor Dr Prabhat Chandra Biswas, DGHS Director Dr Md Nurul Islam and IEDCR Director Dr Kazi Ahmed Zaki attended the meeting as special guests.

item.title: 30 injured as madrasa students clash with police in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
At least 30 people, including 24 madrasa students and six policemen, were injured in a clash between students of Darul Arkam Madrasa and police during a cultural program at the Brahmanbaria Police Lines on Tuesday night.
The incident occurred around 11:30pm inside the Police Lines in the western Medda area of the city after madrasa students reportedly complained about loud music being played at the program.
According to police, madrasa students and locals, the district police were organising the cultural program at the drill shed to mark the arrival of Chittagong Range DIG Abdul Quddus Chowdhury.
Students of the nearby Darul Arkam Madrasa reportedly complained that the loud music was disrupting their studies ahead of examinations scheduled for Wednesday.
Some students went to the Police Lines and asked police personnel to lower the volume. An argument subsequently broke out between the students and police.
As news of the altercation spread, more than 100 madrasa students entered the Police Lines, leading to heightened tensions.
Police then charged with batons to disperse the students, who responded by throwing stones, according to witnesses. The situation subsequently turned violent, with clashes reported inside and outside the Police Lines.
Some students of Darul Arkam Madrasa said they had been preparing for examinations when the loud music began disrupting their studies.
They said they initially approached police and requested that the volume be lowered. Although the music was turned down temporarily, they alleged that the volume was later increased again.
The students alleged that police subsequently charged them with batons when an argument broke out.
The injured students were taken to Brahmanbaria District Sadar Hospital and other hospitals for treatment.
District BNP General Secretary and Upazila Parishad Administrator Sirajul Islam Siraj visited the hospital with party leaders and activists and inquired about the injured students.
Later, madrasa students held a protest procession on several roads in the city and gathered in front of the Press Club for a protest rally. They demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible for the incident.
Around 3am, the Brahmanbaria Qawmi Chhatra Oikya Parishad placed a five-point demand in the presence of Police Superintendent Shah Md Abdur Rouf and District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam Siraj.
The demands include banning loud concerts at the Police Lines that disturb nearby institutions, reviewing CCTV footage and taking action against those responsible, ensuring proper treatment for the injured, implementing the demands by 10am and having the police superintendent take responsibility and issue an unconditional apology.
Brahmanbaria Police Superintendent Shah Md Abdur Rouf, who was present at the program, later visited the madrasa and said the incident resulted from a misunderstanding over the sound from the cultural program.
In a video message, he said the CCTV footage would be reviewed transparently and action would be taken against those found responsible or those who acted excessively.
“Many children have been injured because of a small misunderstanding. This is really unfortunate, and I feel bad about it,” he said.
The police superintendent said arrangements had been made for the injured to receive proper treatment and that necessary financial assistance would also be provided.
He said an investigation committee would be formed, with student representatives included, to examine the incident and ensure justice.
Maulana Sajidur Rahman, principal of Darul Arkam Madrasa and secretary general of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, also urged students and others to remain calm.
In a video message, he said the police superintendent and District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam Siraj had visited the madrasa and discussed the students’ demands.
He said the police superintendent had assured them that exemplary action would be taken against those responsible after reviewing the video footage.
Sajidur Rahman urged students, ulema and others concerned to remain calm, saying the matter would be properly investigated and justice ensured based on the footage.

item.title: BIP: Unplanned urbanisation pushes Dhaka near bottom of livability index
item.description:
Dhaka now ranks 171st among 173 cities on the Global Livability Index, planners said Tuesday warning that unplanned urbanisation, environmental degradation and weak governance have pushed the capital to one of the lowest livability levels in the world.
Speaking at a press conference titled "Dhaka City's Livability: Challenges and Roadmap for Planned Solutions," organised by the Bangladesh Institute of Planners (BIP) at its conference hall in Planners Tower, BIP President Muhammad Ariful Islam said transport, air and noise pollution, waterlogging, shrinking green space, public health risks and weak social inclusion are all directly tied to the city's planning failures.
He said Dhaka ranks 18th among the world's most polluted cities.
Of the roughly 56 canals the city once had, only 26 survive in any recognisable form, while 48 areas have been identified as waterlogging-prone due to encroachment on canals and wetlands and poor drainage, he said.
Ariful Islam said unplanned billboards and lighting are damaging the cityscape and road safety, he added, while rising building density and poor waste management are fuelling dengue and chikungunya risks.
Only 7.99 percent of the city's 99.29 square kilometres is green space, he said, far short of what a livable city needs.
On transport, Ariful said Dhaka loses about 50 lakh working hours annually to congestion, at an estimated economic cost of Tk 37,000 crore.
He said around 1,765 tonnes of waste, 27 percent of total generation, goes uncollected daily, worsening waterlogging and mosquito breeding.
BIP General Secretary Mohammad Mosleh Uddin Hasan said Dhaka is heading toward its lowest-ever livability level due to poor implementation of existing plans and institutional weakness.
Planner Adil Muhammad Khan raised concerns over footpath encroachment, illegal businesses, extortion, and political influence in urban management while planner AKM Riaz Uddin noted that despite declining livability, migration to Dhaka continues because other regions lack jobs and services.
Speakers agreed that Dhaka's crisis stems from interlinked failures in environment, land use, transport, health and waste management, calling for long-term, coordinated national planning.

item.title: AIUB hosts first-ever ‘QS Bangladesh Forum 2026’
item.description:
The first-ever QS Bangladesh Forum 2026 was held on Monday, August 17, at the Sheraton Dhaka, with the aim of advancing the future of higher education in Bangladesh, strengthening global standards, and enhancing the position of Bangladeshi universities in the international arena.
The forum was hosted by the American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB) and organized by QS (Quacquarelli Symonds), with support from the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) and the Association of Private Universities of Bangladesh (APUB).
Themed “Benchmark Bangladesh: Building World-Class Universities Through Global Standards,” the forum brought together key stakeholders from Bangladesh’s higher education sector.
The inaugural session was attended by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, MP, as chief guest.
Prof Mamun Ahmed, chairman of the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh, attended as guest of honour.
In his address, the minister highlighted the need to introduce PhD programs at private universities and indicated that initiatives would soon be taken in this regard.
Questioning why private universities should not be permitted to offer PhD programs, he emphasized the importance of creating broader opportunities for advanced research in the private higher education sector.
Referring to the development of private universities in Bangladesh since 1992, he stressed that, by 2026, the country must create greater opportunities for advanced research at private universities.
Highlighting the importance of research, he said that Bangladesh needs cross-border education and stronger research capacity in private universities.
He also noted that the country has no shortage of teachers and researchers, with thousands of researchers contributing to national development through knowledge, expertise, and “Made in Bangladesh” capabilities.
Prof Mamun Ahmed, chairman of UGC, said that Bangladeshi private universities still have significant room for improvement in global university rankings.
He emphasized the need for universities to take a leading role in improving academic quality and making their institutions more attractive to students. Such efforts, he noted, could help attract more international students to Bangladesh for higher education.
QS representatives also addressed the forum, including Ashwin Fernandes, vice president – strategic and international engagement, QS; Jason Newman, chief commercial officer, QS; and Rami Awad, director of regional partnerships, QS.
The welcome address was delivered by Ishtiaque Abedin, founding member of the board of trustees of AIUB and secretary general of APUB.
Md Sabur Khan, president of APUB, also addressed the forum.
The vote of thanks was delivered by Nadia Anwar, founding member and chairperson of the board of trustees, AIUB.
Following the inaugural session, three dedicated sessions were held on QS Rankings Methodology, QS ranking landscape of Bangladesh, and the QS Rankings 2028 Cycle.
The forum also featured two high-level panel discussions involving Vice-Chancellors from leading universities across Bangladesh: “From Campus to Capability: Closing Bangladesh’s Future Skills Gap in the AI Era” and “Accelerating Digital Transformation in Higher Education.”
The panel discussions focused on the future skills required by students in the age of artificial intelligence, aligning education with industry needs, leveraging technology in higher education, and accelerating digital transformation across universities.
The closing session featured a vote of thanks by Carmen Zita Lamagna, former vice chancellor, academic adviser, and member of the board of trustees, AIUB.
The QS Bangladesh Forum 2026 placed particular emphasis on the internationalization of higher education, enhancing the global visibility of research, improving student outcomes and capabilities, and strengthening international partnerships.
With the QS World University Rankings 2028 cycle ahead, discussions also focused on developing a common, practical, and strategic roadmap for universities to prepare for and improve their global competitiveness.

item.title: Hop Lun partners with Brac Healthcare to host employee wellness camp
item.description:
Hop Lun Apparel Limited recently organized a comprehensive ‘Seasonal Disease Prevention and Awareness Session’ at its factory premises in partnership with Brac Healthcare.
The initiative provided workers with free medical check-ups as well as expert guidance on disease prevention, hygiene, and healthy living in order to safeguard their overall health and well-being.
During the session, workers underwent screenings for blood sugar, blood pressure and oxygen saturation levels.
Any individuals diagnosed with adverse health conditions were immediately provided medical treatment by Hop Lun’s in-house medical team.
Additionally, two healthcare professionals from Brac healthcare conducted interactive sessions with the workers, advising workers on preventing common illnesses, knowing when to consult a doctor, and effective ways to maintain overall health at home and in the workplace.
They discussed about how health and work are deeply connected and how personal physical fitness is key to both professional performance and personal life.
Dr Tahmid Hasan Probad, manager, QA and patient experience at Brac Healthcare Ltd, stated: “Through this partnership, we wanted to deliver quality healthcare access for workers and create health awareness among them. We firmly believe that a healthy worker thrives in the workplace with greater ease.”
Gulshan Ara, social initiatives head, Hop Lun Bangladesh, added: “The physical and mental well-being of our workers is one of our top priorities. With this initiative, we aimed to make essential medical support more accessible for our workers and to equip them with the knowledge they need in order to maintain proper health.”
Hop Lun Apparel Limited remains dedicated to prioritizing worker well-being and continuing such health and welfare initiatives across its facilities in the future.

item.title: Bangladesh, IOM launch new initiative to combat cyber-enabled human trafficking
item.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM-UN Migration) and the Economic Relations Division (ERD) of Ministry of Finance of Bangladesh have signed a 24-month project to strengthen Bangladesh's efforts to prevent and respond to human trafficking facilitated through digital technologies.
The project, "Countering Cyber-Enabled Human Trafficking Through Technology", funded by the IOM Development Fund, will be implemented by IOM Bangladesh in partnership with the Ministry of Home Affairs. The project aims to support longer-term efforts to prevent cyber-enabled human trafficking in Bangladesh. Its findings and training resources are expected to contribute to future policy and program development and to strengthen existing national and inter-agency efforts to combat trafficking, said a press release on Monday.
Responding to growing concerns over the use of social media, online platforms, job portals and other digital technologies by traffickers to target, recruit, control and exploit people, the project will focus on three key areas including building evidence and knowledge, strengthening law enforcement capacity and improving digital literacy in communities. The agreement was signed by Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky, secretary of ERD, and Dr Laura Tomm Bonde, chief of mission of IOM Bangladesh, in the presence of AKM Sohel, additional secretary and wing chief of UN Wing, ERD, and representatives of relevant government agencies including Ministry of Home Affairs and IOM, according to an ERD press release.
"Technology is transforming the way people communicate, seek employment and connect with opportunities, but it can also be exploited by traffickers," said Dr Laura Tomm Bonde. "This project will help strengthen the evidence, skills and community awareness needed to ensure that technology becomes part of the solution rather than a tool for exploitation," she added.
"The project will contribute to the Government of Bangladesh's efforts to prevent the misuse of technology for human trafficking while promoting technology as a means to counter human trafficking. Its overall outcome is to enable government stakeholders and communities to take informed action to prevent, respond to and mitigate the risks of cyber-enabled human trafficking," Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky emphasized.

item.title: Chamber court upholds bail for ex-chief justice Khairul Haque

item.title: 3 sentenced to death for killing AIUB student in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Narayanganj court on Monday sentenced three muggers to death for killing Wazed Alam Shimanto, a student of American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), in 2024.
Narayanganj District and Sessions’ Judge Abu Shamim Azad pronounced the verdict.
The condemned convicts are Anik, Akash Khan and Chandi Babu.
According to the prosecution, three muggers intercepted Shimanto, a 2nd year student of the AIUB Department of Computer Science, in front of Morgan Girls’ High School at Deubhog of Narayanganj city around 6:00am on December 12, 2024.
At one stage, the hoodlums stabbed Shimanto indiscriminately and left the place after snatching his bag and mobile phone set.
The victim was sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries two days later.
Shimanto’s father Hazi Alam filed a case at Sadar Police Station in this regard.
Police arrested the trio from different parts of the district following the incident. All of them gave confessional statements before the court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

item.title: PM’s Adviser: 'Mob culture' will not be tolerated
item.description:
The government will not tolerate “mob culture” in the country and will enforce law to prevent such incidents, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Public Administration Affairs Ismail Zabihullah said on Monday.
“Mob culture is undesirable whenever it occurs. We hope there will be no mob culture, and it should never happen,” he said while responding to questions from journalists at an exchange of views at the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon to mark 180 days of the government.
Asked about allegations that mob incidents continued after the ouster of Sheikh Hasina and that law enforcement agencies remained largely inactive in dealing with such incidents, the adviser said he had no clear example of a recent incident of the kind seen during the final period the interim government.
“There is no such mob culture as was seen toward the end of the interim government. However, we can assure you that this kind of mob culture will not be tolerated,” said Zabihullah, also a BNP Standing Committee member.
He stressed that the country would be governed according to law and that the government would enforce it.
Prime Minister’s Political Adviser and another BNP Standing Committee member Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, who joined the discussion, said the extent of mob culture has declined significantly.
He said such a culture emerged partly because of political support and that there had often been an indirect political influence behind such incidents.
“As the rule of law becomes stronger, mob violence will decline,” Rizvi said, adding that the government’s commitment to the rule of law would help create an environment in which such incidents would decrease further.
Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson Mahadi Amin presented statistics on the government’s activities and achievements over the past 180 days.
The event was moderated by Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibli. PM’s Political Adviser Nazrul Islam Khan, Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapan and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon also spoke at the program.
Ministers and advisers responded to questions from journalists on various issues.
State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, State Ministe for Information and Broadcasting Yaser Khan Chowdhury, Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir, Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant on Health SM Ziauddin Haider, Special Assistant on Environment, Forest and Climate Affairs Saimum Parvez and Chief Coordinator at the Prime Minister’s Office Prof SM Abdul Awal, among others, attended the program.
